# Baruch Chapter 5 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Baruch 5 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/BAR_005_page_001.jpg

---

**1** Jerusalem, take off your mourning clothes, your grief-worn garments. Put on the beauty of God's own glory — and wear it forever.

**2** Wrap yourself in God's righteousness like a double cloak. Set on your head the crown of the Eternal's glory.

**3** For God is going to display your splendor to every nation on earth.

**4** And God will give you a new name that will last forever: Peace of Righteousness, Glory of Godliness.

**5** Rise up, Jerusalem. Stand on the heights. Look east — and watch your children coming home. They are streaming back from every point where the sun rises to every point where it sets, called back at the word of the Holy One, their hearts full of joy because God has remembered them.

**6** They left you on foot, marched away by their enemies. But God is bringing them back to you carried in honor, like royalty on a throne.

**7** God himself has commanded it: every towering mountain must be brought low, every ancient hill must bow down, every valley must be filled in — so that Israel can walk safely home, in the glory of God.

**8** The forest trees and every sweet-scented tree will spread their shade over Israel, at God's command, for the journey.

**9** For God will lead Israel home in joy, his glory lighting the way, his mercy and his righteousness surrounding them.

---
*PNEUMA notes: This nine-verse chapter is one of the most beautiful passages in the Deuterocanon — a pure lyric of restoration. It reverses everything that came before: the mourning garments (4:20) become glory-robes; the children sent away in tears (4:11, 23) return in joy; the mother who stood weeping now stands on the heights watching them come home. The Isaiah 40 echo in v.7 is structural, not decorative — the new Exodus will surpass the first. The "double cloak" of v.2 is a mark of royal dignity and covenant honor. The new name in v.4 ("Peace of Righteousness / Glory of Godliness") is a formal divine renaming, like the renaming of Abram, Jacob, and Jerusalem itself in Isa 62:4. The chapter ends not with a cry but with a procession — God leading his people in light.*
